tested_question: When fixed C_tes assumptions drive large changes in the fitted Magnicon+c2 transfer, is the final observable fitted ASD shape also anchor-sensitive, or do detector dynamics/white compensate?

physical_anchor_context.C_tes_source_semantics: TES bilayer geometry x density x specific heat; independent of the noise fit but not direct calorimetry

layer_semantics.full_fitted_ASD: best-fit pre-analysis ASD including the independently profiled post-filter white floor
layer_semantics.zero_post_filter_white_ASD: same best-fit detector/readout state with only the profiled post-filter white term set to zero
layer_semantics.readout_transfer: Magnicon 10 kHz Bessel times phenomenological c2 numerator

cross_day_geometric_mean_anchor_sensitiv.semantics: For each C_tes anchor, geometric mean of the separately normalized 12/06 and 12/05 shapes, followed by anchor-to-anchor comparison.

interpretation.guardrail: The full fitted ASD is the observable model comparison; the zero-post-filter-white spectrum is a decomposition diagnostic, not a separately measured quantity. Small full-ASD anchor sensitivity alongside large readout-transfer sensitivity would demonstrate non-identifiability/cancellation, not identify which decomposition is physically correct. Rows where c2 hits a configured bound are censored and excluded from the primary finite-shape classification.
